data.title: CertiK: Crypto Industry Losses Hit Record $9.2 Billion in 2026
data.description: CertiK's live data dashboard shows cumulative crypto industry losses reached a record $9.2 billion in 2026. According to ChainCatcher, $3.03 billion in assets were frozen or recovered in October, bringing adjusted losses for the month to $3.47 billion.

data.title: Uniswap TJAR Fee Conversion System Opens to All Apps and Covers Seven Chains
data.description: Uniswap said on X that its TJAR fee conversion system is now available to all applications. According to Odaily, the system lets applications convert fees received in different tokens into a designated token. It processed more than $15.3 million in conversions last month and now operates across seven chains. Robinhood uses TJAR through the Uniswap API and receives fees in USDC and USDG.

data.title: AI | AI Enthusiasm Slumps as Tech Earnings Add to Market Concerns
data.description: AI enthusiasm is collapsing, and technology earnings have added to concerns weighing on a stock market facing doubts about heavy artificial-intelligence spending, according to Bloomberg. A series of technology giants reported earnings over the last two weeks, a period that was expected to bring clarity.

data.title: GEOPOLITICS | Kaja Kallas Warns Against Normalizing Russia Internationally
data.description:
EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas said Russia is escalating its war in Ukraine and is not serious about peace, criticizing Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov’s remarks at the G20 foreign ministers’ meeting in Atlanta, according to Bloomberg. Kallas warned against normalizing Moscow on the international stage.

In an interview with Bloomberg This Weekend host David Gura, Kallas also called for a diplomatic solution to tensions with Iran and discussed deepening the EU’s relationship with Canada through increased cooperation on trade, energy and defense.

data.title: Trump Promised to Slash Energy Costs, but Gasoline, Diesel and Jet Fuel Soared
data.description: According to CNBC, President Donald Trump pledged to bring gasoline below $2 a gallon within his first year in office, but the national average stood at $4.20 a gallon on Friday, nearly 40% above the same period last year. Diesel reached $6.32 a gallon, up about 70% over the year, while high jet-fuel costs have led airlines to raise fares. GasBuddy petroleum analyst Patrick De Haan said gas and diesel prices were on track to be the highest ever on an election day. Fuel prices have risen amid disruptions linked to the conflict involving Iran, including reduced oil flows through the Strait of Hormuz. Trump issued an order allowing truckers to use tax-exempt off-road diesel on U.S. highways and announced an $8 billion relief program for farmers affected by high fuel prices.

data.title: PRECIOUS METALS | Gold Options Show Cautious Sentiment as Put Positions Rise More Than Calls
data.description: According to Jin10, recent options activity shows gold market sentiment turning notably cautious: call positions continued to increase, indicating that rebound expectations have not fully faded, while put positions grew more strongly as investors increased protection against further declines.

data.title: Pop-Up Super PACs Spend $637 Million in 2026 Midterm Races
data.description: According to CNBC, 22 super PACs formed in the final 10 weeks before Election Day had reported roughly $637 million in independent expenditures on House and Senate races by Oct. 29, about one-sixth of all such spending in congressional races this election cycle. Republican-linked groups spent about twice as much as Democratic-linked groups. Many began spending before filing their first regular reports identifying their donors.

data.title: Russia Extends Restrictions on Most Diesel Exports Through January
data.description: Russia extended a general ban on diesel exports by producers through the end of January, while allowing some volumes to reach the global market, according to Bloomberg.

data.title: Rivian and Ford Expand 3D Printing to Cut Costs and Speed Production
data.description: According to CNBC, Rivian Automotive and Ford Motor are expanding 3D printing across their manufacturing operations to reduce costs and shorten production times. Rivian has spent more than $5 million on 3D-printing machines, with materials costing about $1.7 million annually. Jared Beck, the company’s head of additive manufacturing, said the machines typically pay for themselves within a year and can cut parts-production times from weeks to days or hours. Rivian is also adding machines for printing flexible silicone parts and plans to let employees print parts on demand. Ford’s 3D-printing program has more than 200 machines, and the company expects to have labs at more than 23 plants by the end of this year.

data.title: Humans Still Do Work Behind Some AI Agents
data.description: According to CNBC, AI agents from companies including Meta and OpenAI still struggle to reliably complete tasks involving phone calls, scheduling and real-world judgment, leading some startups to bring in human contractors. Duckbill recently launched an API that lets companies building personal agents delegate tasks to workers, while Dazzle AI uses contractors when its technology flags a task it cannot handle. Dazzle CEO Marissa Mayer said current models can provide useful recommendations but may fail at complex tasks, and Duckbill CEO Meghan Joyce said human judgment remains important. Meta currently does not use humans to complete users’ Muse requests.

data.title: Norwegian Firm Has $100 Million at Stake in Mercuria-Baltic Exchange Case
data.description: A Norwegian firm has $100 million riding on Mercuria Energy Group’s case against the Baltic Exchange, according to Bloomberg. Mercuria’s lawyers presented the commodity company’s arguments this week in a packed London courtroom, where a group of Norwegian businessmen listened from the back.
